To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Marangoni instability is affected by the additive properties and the gas phase properties, and there is a meaningful relationship between the absorbate Marangoninumber and the modified Biotnumber for the onset of the instability.

there is a critical value of mass transfer coefficient in gas phase and the additive Marangon number MaA and relative surface diffusivities of additive RA act as the stabilizers and the destabilizer, respectively for the onset Marangoni convections.

the combined absorbent Marangoni number is linearly proportional to the modified Bionumber, the additive Marangoninumber acts as a stabilizer, and the relative surface diffusion of additive acts as a destabilizer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a horizontal fluid layer heated from below and cooled from above with an additive in the liquid phase.
the effects of additive on the absorption process.
the effect of additive and the mass transfer coefficient of gas phase on Marangoni convec- tion and absorption process for a horizontal liquid layer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Marangoni convections are more easily excited in the case of a low Biot number and a high relative surface diffusibility of additive.
there is an optimum value of the relative surface diffusive of additive which is about 0.5 in the present study for the most unstable state.
the additive is not always beneficial for the absorption process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the additive properties are the important parameters to control the onset of Maragoni convection and hence the absorption process.

the combined absorbates Marangoni number and the modified Biot numbers are the important parameters to control the absorption process and that the additive properties are also important for the onset of the Marangoni instability.
the combined absorbent Marangoni number is linearly related with the modified Biot and there is critical modified Biot to cause the most instable state of the liquid layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the additive properties can be utilized as an efficient control parameter to manipulate the absorption process in a liquid layer.
the Marangoni convections are not only caused by the surface tension gradient induced by the absorption process but also by the additive properties.
the additive can be used to enhance the mass transfer rate in the gas phase and also to stabilize the liquid layer.
